reason: Compared the complete source def:gauss and its inherited generic-polygon and cyclic-representative conventions with SM.gauss_definition and the actual construction bodies. TraversalPoint is exactly ZMod n times the half-open real interval [0,1), not a closed interval with duplicated adjacent endpoints. traversalEvaluation is the source point P i+t*edge P i. The real key i.val+t gives the within-edge parameter order and the successive edge-block order at a numerical cut; traversalBetween is its strict ternary cyclic order with all three possible wraps. Its agreement with the constructed circular order is proved. Starting at residue zero rather than source label one changes only the cyclic cut, not orientation. Visits are the dependent sum of an actual crossing and one of its two edge indices. Their positions use the previously defined crossing parameters, with strict interior bounds and proved evaluation at the actual unique crossing point. visits_per_crossing, card_visit and card_crossing identify the finite visit inventory with exactly two visits for every actual unordered crossing and total size 2|X(P)|. Genericity proves actual visit positions and keys injective; this is not assumed as a property of an arbitrary word. gaussList is the independently constructed sort of all visits by that geometric key. The aggregate proves completeness, no duplicate visits, strict sorting and the exact length. gaussCycle is its image in mathlib Cycle, whose inspected definition is List modulo IsRotated only. gaussWord maps each visit to its actual crossing identity; it retains repeated crossing letters and has both the required total length and exactly two occurrences of each crossing, measured in its rotation-independent multiset. The construction neither identifies reversal with rotation nor quotients by arbitrary permutations or renamings. The full aggregate also covers representative independence. traversalShiftEquiv maps every half-open traversal point by i maps to i-a with inverse shift by -a, and traversalBetween_shift proves preservation of cyclic order for all traversal points, not merely crossing visits. traversalEvaluation_shift and the visit position/parameter shift laws preserve the actual geometry. visitShiftEquiv is constructed from the actual crossingShiftEquiv and its two-edge fibre equivalence, with a proved inverse/bijection and correct crossing projection. The shifted traversal key subtracts the cut and adds n exactly to points before it, using the proved bounds 0<=key<n. SortedCut proves that the transported old list and the independently sorted shifted list differ by rotation: it splits the old sorted list at the cut, shows the high-then-low concatenation is sorted by the shifted key, and identifies it with the target list through equal inventory and sorted-list uniqueness. Thus gaussCycle_shift and gaussWord_shift compare independently built constructions; they do not define the target as a convenient rotation or assume the desired invariance. Crossing labels are transported through the genuine crossingShiftEquiv. Empty crossing sets are admitted throughout: no nonempty-list, chosen-first-visit or chosen-crossing hypothesis occurs, and sorting/rotation/cardinality assertions correctly give the empty cycle and word. Repeated crossing letters remain distinct visits before projection. The only inputs to the aggregate are the inherited n>=3, the concrete tuple P and Generic P. There is no arbitrary input word, graph, root, label oracle, order witness or desired-law assumption. The semantic dependency inventory binds every traversal, visit, sorting, cycle, word and transport definition giving these assertions meaning. All 16 inspected local supporting files match the passed development receipt; the eight previously accepted crossing/geometry files are unchanged. The receipt audited 454 declarations with only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound and explicitly does not accept the overall stage. This review certifies exactly the original def:gauss row; it does not certify interlacement, the visible signature or visible-signature constancy, and supporting lemmas do not add original claims.

Traversal circle: TraversalPoint n = ZMod n × Set.Ico 0 1 (Traversal.lean:12) is the source set of pairs (i,t), i ∈ Z/n, t ∈ [0,1); traversalEvaluation P (i,t) = P i + t • edge P i with edge P i = P(i+1) - P i = ℓ_i (Polygon.lean:49-52), and the theorem asserts this pointwise. Cyclic order: traversalKey (i,t) = i.val + t (Traversal.lean:17) with the asserted characterization key p < key q ↔ i-block order or same edge with t < t' (source's two generating clauses at the cut label 0), and traversalBetween (Traversal.lean:73-76) is the strict ternary cyclic order of that linear order with all three wraps (= LinearOrder.toCircularOrder, Traversal.lean:78); the theorem asserts its invariance under relabelling traversalShift a (p.1 - a, p.2), so the cyclic order is cut-independent as a cyclic order must be. Visits: Visit P = Σ c : Crossing P, {i // i ∈ c.val} (GaussVisits.lean:17) where Crossing P = {s // ∃ i j, s = {i,j} ∧ remote i j ∧ (E_i ∩ E_j).Nonempty} (Crossings.lean:12-15) is exactly X(P) of def:crossings; each crossing has two visits (card 2 by remoteness); visitPosition v = (i, t_ij) with t_ij = crossingParameter, the parameter with crossingPoint c = μ_i + t ℓ_i (Crossings.lean:41,70-78), unique under G1; the theorem asserts 0 < t_ij < 1 and evaluation at the crossing point, and injectivity of visitPosition under Generic (so the visits are distinct points of Γ(P)). Gauss word: gaussList = sort of all visits by visitKey = traversalKey ∘ visitPosition (GaussWord.lean:17-24); gaussCycle = its Cycle (Mathlib List modulo rotation) and gaussWord = gaussCycle.map Sigma.fst, i.e. the cyclic sequence of the visits in the order of Γ(P), each labelled by its crossing (GaussWord.lean:84-89); the theorem asserts completeness, nodup, strict sorting, length 2|X(P)| (Nat.card (Crossing P)), each crossing occurring exactly twice, rotation independence, and σ-equivariance (shift 1 = σ, Polygon.lean:22) of gaussCycle/gaussWord through the genuine crossingShiftEquiv/visitShiftEquiv (old edge i ↦ i - a, consistent with shift a P = fun i => P (i + a)). No arbitrary word, root, or order is an input; nothing is vacuous (only P and Generic P are assumed). All 16 reviewed file hashes and the source hash in reviews/def-gauss.json match the current files. The Lean objects denote the printed traversal circle, visits and Gauss word; the existing review's conclusion is confirmed, and its reasoning agrees with mine.
stronger_than_source: The theorem additionally proves facts the printed definition only presupposes or that follow from lem:crossing-test: injectivity of visit positions (distinct crossing points), 0 < t_ij < 1, exact length 2|X(P)| and exactly two occurrences of every crossing in the word (GaussDefinition.lean:44-58). These are well-definedness/consistency checks, not extra hypotheses.

Shift-equivariance of the traversal cyclic order, gaussCycle and gaussWord under every cyclic relabelling a : ZMod n is proved (GaussDefinition.lean:59-69); the source only records the general convention (def:polygon remark) that every notion is shift-invariant.

The cyclic order is realized concretely (key i.val + t, ternary betweenness with all three wraps) rather than described by generating clauses; the asserted key characterization and shift invariance show it is the source's cyclic order, with the cut at residue 0 instead of label 1 (a cut choice that does not affect any cyclic object).
